messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for service=infra-inference-queue warmup-backlog (PAGER: P2249) — queue length > 12k, sustained for 2m, autoscaler not scaling

pagerduty: page triggered and sent to eng-oncall -> jamie

jamie (oncall): ack'd - i'm on it :hand:

jamie (oncall): quick triage — looking at /metrics and queue dashboard, backlog spiked at 14:22 UTC, avg processing latency jumped from 200ms -> 1.8s, some 504s showing up. autoscaler last scaled 25m ago and has had no new nodes provisioned.

megan (platform): noticed nodegroup quota errors in the provisioner logs earlier: "insufficient quota for instance launch" repeated. could be hitting cloud provider quota or our spot bid failover path.

leo (eng-sre): can you paste the autoscaler logs? might be an API limit or metrics-server failing to respond.

jamie (oncall): grabbing logs now, pasting relevant snippets:

```
2025-11-03T14:18:12Z autoscaler controller: reconcile loop start
2025-11-03T14:18:13Z autoscaler: evaluate scaling: desired_replicas=120 current=48
2025-11-03T14:18:13Z cloudprovider: launch instances failed: QuotaExceeded: requested 72 cores, available 0
2025-11-03T14:18:14Z autoscaler: fallthrough to fallbackPolicy=burst-fail
```

jamie (oncall): so autoscaler tried to scale but cloud rejected. queue prefix warmup caching also stressed KV-cache which made per-request processing heavier.

megan (platform): ok that matches what i see in infra provisioning. we have a pending quota increase request but ETA is ~1h. short-term options: 1) manual scale within existing node pool (if any capacity), 2) spin up dedicated reserved pool (approved for emergency), 3) activate smart-routing fallback to smaller model variant for non-enterprise tenants.

jamie (oncall): low-friction action: try manual scale on any available nodegroup and enable fallback routing for public traffic. I'll coordinate with CS for enterprise customers.

leo (eng-sre): also check KEDA/HPA metrics — if metrics-server is down, autoscaler can't see CPU/RPS and will avoid scaling. run `kubectl get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes` to verify.

jamie (oncall): running that now...

```
$ kubectl get --raw /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes
Error from server (ServiceUnavailable): the server is currently unable to handle the request
```

jamie (oncall): metrics-server returning 503 — that's why HPA/KEDA didn't trigger. may be degraded after control-plane upgrade patch earlier.

megan (platform): i'm going to trigger the emergency reserved pool spin-up and also open fallback on public routes. tagging infra-oncall to watch.

megan (platform): command i'm running: 

```
# spin up reserved pool (emergency) — uses pre-approved image
infractl pool create --name reserved-emergency-01 --type g4dn.xlarge --count 24 --labels reserved=emergency
```

megan (platform): infractl shows provisioning started, launching 24 instances (spot-hotfallback disabled)

pagerduty: escalation timer set: escalate to eng-sre lead in 20m if not acknowledged by SRE team

jamie (oncall): meanwhile enabling model-fallback for non-SLA tenants: toggling route via Console -> Projects -> routing -> fallback-policy -> enable smaller-variant. Doing a canary to 10% first.

jamie (oncall): console changes applied, canary 10% live. hoping that reduces overall token pressure while infra comes up.

leo (eng-sre): good. i'll watch queue length and pod readiness. also checking node pools: `kubectl get nodes` shows many nodes NotReady due to kubelet restart churn from recent control-plane patch. that's probably compounding things.

jamie (oncall): manual scale attempt on worker deployment to 80 replicas within current pool:

```
kubectl scale deploy inference-worker --replicas=80 -n prod
kubectl get deploy inference-worker -n prod
NAME                READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
inference-worker    80/80   80           12          6m
```

jamie (oncall): interesting, READY shows only 12 available — pods stuck in Pending due to insufficient nodes. scaling helped create pod objects but they can't land.

megan (platform): reserved pool instances are coming up, cloud console shows 12/24 in READY state. provisioning logs: network plugin delayed on a subset due to image pull throttling. i'm increasing parallel pulls.

leo (eng-sre): re KEDA metrics — once metrics-server recovers, autoscaler should resume normal behavior. for now we have manual scale + reserved pool. also recommend applying a temporary token-rate limit for best-effort tenants to protect SLA customers.

jamie (oncall): applying rate limit in gateway: `rate-limit set project=public default=20rps`

cs-bot: Notifying Customer Success: high-impact incident — some customers may experience degraded latency/timeouts. Sending alert to CS channel and creating a CS ticket: CS-98742

megan (platform): reserved pool now at 20/24 ready, kubelet registration done for new nodes. starting to schedule pending pods.

jamie (oncall): monitoring queue length — it's dropping from 12k -> 4.1k over 9m. p50 latency back to 300ms, p95 at 1.2s. fewer 504s.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident updated: acknowledged by jamie, remediation in progress, escalation canceled.

leo (eng-sre): can we confirm customer impact? jamie, any enterprise customers hit hard?

jamie (oncall): quick estimate from logs: ~2100 requests failed with 504 across 30m window. mapping to customers shows ~9 tenants affected; one enterprise account (acct_2213) saw multiple timeouts on their batch jobs — i've flagged CS to prioritize.

cs-bot: CS Slack thread created: https://redwood.example/cs/CS-98742 — sent initial customer-facing note to acct_2213.

jamie (oncall): mitigation summary: manual reserved pool spin-up + model fallback for non-SLA tenants + gateway rate-limiting. queue draining and tail latency improving.

megan (platform): filing emergency follow-up ticket to request immediate quota increase with cloud provider (we'll include autoscaler and metrics-server notes). also rolling back the control-plane patch to debug kubelet churn (postmortem will include timeline).

leo (eng-sre): assigning postmortem owners: jamie (oncall) for remediation timeline, megan for infra provisioning, leo for autoscaler/metrics diagnosis. I'll create the RCA doc and link.

jamie (oncall): handing off to leo for deeper RCA and follow-up. i'll stay reachable for 30m then go rotation. please update incident tracker: INC-2025-4321

incident-bot: Incident marked as Mitigated by jamie (oncall) at 14:52 UTC — queue below threshold and errors returning to baseline.

jamie (oncall): final note for the thread — immediate customer impact: degraded latency for ~9 tenants, ~2k failed requests, one enterprise with transient timeouts. mitigation actions: manual reserved pool spin-up, model fallback, gateway rate-limiting. Follow-ups: quota increase request, metrics-server stability fix, control-plane patch rollback analysis, and PM/customer outreach.

megan (platform): thanks all — i'll update the infra incident ticket with logs and timeline.

leo (eng-sre): i'll open the RCA and schedule the postmortem meeting for tomorrow.

jamie (oncall): handing off now. closing thread for live triage. :white_check_mark:
